claims.text: At stage-1, ListByCustomerAsync(customerId) was db.Orders.Where(customer).Include(o => o.Customer).OrderBy(o => o.Id).ToListAsync() with no paging, returning List<Order>; Customer then mapped password_hash, gone at stage-2.

A query that returns entity instances fetches all mapped columns of the entity, and Include loads the whole related entity, so the stage-1 list loaded every mapped column of Order and Customer, including email and password_hash.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Performance > Efficient querying > Project only properties you need; Querying > Eager loading

claims.text: EF Core translates a Select inside the query into SQL that fetches only the values the projection uses; nothing is sent until ToListAsync() runs, and it then builds one OrderSummary per returned row.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Efficient querying > Project only properties you need ('pulls back only the needed columns')

claims.text: Accessing a navigation property (o.Customer.FullName) inside Select makes EF Core add the JOIN to the related table itself; no Include is needed, and Include is ignored when the query does not return the entity type it started with.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Querying > Eager loading (Include ignored when projecting); observed in efcore-sql.txt at stage-2

claims.text: If the result set of a query contains no entity types, no tracking is done; so a projection into OrderSummary records is not tracked without AsNoTracking().
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Tracking vs. No-Tracking Queries > Tracking and custom projections

claims.text: The properties of a positional record (record OrderSummary(int Id, ...)) are init-only: they cannot be set after the object is created.
claims.source_hint: C# docs: Records > Positional syntax for property definition (init-only properties)

claims.text: EF Core's change tracking works with entity instances only, so projected records cannot be changed and saved back through SaveChanges.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Efficient querying ('EF's change tracking only works with entity instances')

claims.text: At stage-2 ListByCustomerAsync filters by customer and afterId, orders by Id, takes limit, selects new OrderSummary(o.Id, o.Status, o.Customer!.FullName) with no Include; the inner query holds the WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT, the outer one the JOIN.
DonHang.Domain/OrderSummary.cs declares public sealed record OrderSummary(int Id, string Status, string CustomerName); it lives in DonHang.Domain so IOrderRepository need not know DonHang.Api's DTOs.
At stage-2 OrdersController.List copies each OrderSummary into an OrderSummaryDto(Id, Status, CustomerName) for the JSON response.

The captured command selects o0.id, o0.status, c.full_name from an inner query on orders (id, customer_id, status) with INNER JOIN customers ON o0.customer_id = c.id; no other customers column is selected (c.id is only in the join).
Customer at stage-2 has the mapped properties Id, FullName, Email, City and IdentitySubject.
Use a projection for reading data to build a response, and load tracked entities when the data will be changed and saved.
